acceptance: The culprit is the head of the first red run after the last green completed run (the start of the red streak); a test covers a two-run streak whose second PR is innocent.
A `fix/revert-*` branch that reverts the streak's first red commit is exempt; a revert of a commit outside the streak is not.
The refusal message names the streak's first culprit PR and its revert command.
context: Delivered in merged PR #3415: red_streak_start returns the first red completed run after the last green one (pending/cancelled runs do not break the streak); fix/revert-* exemption and is_reverted use that streak-start commit; fetch window widens 30/100/300/1000 and fails closed when the streak start cannot be established. Tests include the #3200/#3220 scenario. Not verified against live GitHub runs.
description:
`scripts/trunk_revert.py` `arm_gate` (`:150-170`) takes the newest completed red Trunk run (`red_trunk_run`, `:99-107`), names the PR merged at that run's head as the culprit, and exempts only a `fix/revert-*` branch whose commits say `This reverts commit <that head>`. When a failure persists across later merges, the newest red run's head is a later, innocent PR. The gate then tells the operator to revert that PR and refuses the revert of the commit that broke Trunk. `is_reverted` checks the same newest head, so merging the real revert does not clear the gate until a new Trunk run completes.

Observed 2026-10-21: #3200 (4e8118c98) turned Trunk red (run 39549351208). #3220 merged next and its Trunk run (39555893700) failed the same way. `make pr-arm` on the revert of #3200 (#3223, branch `fix/revert-3200`) refused with `the newest completed trunk.yml run failed at PR #3220 ... Merge a revert (make trunk-revert PR=3220)`. Related: trunk-red-stops-further-merges.
